record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: For a set of reals X, the δ-property means that for every open ω-cover U of X, the space X belongs to the closure of U under the lim inf operation. The property (Ω over Γ) means that every open ω-cover of X contains an open γ-subcover. Are these two properties equivalent?

evidence.quote: Is the δ-property equivalent to (Ω Γ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a set of real numbers (equivalently, a separable metrizable zero-dimensional space). 

Recall the following definitions:
- An open cover U of X is an ω-cover if X is not a member of U and every finite subset of X is contained in some U ∈ U.
- An open cover U of X is a γ-cover if U is infinite and every x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U.
- The lim inf operator on a family U of subsets of X is defined by liminf(U) = ⋃_{V ⊆ U infinite} ⋂ V; equivalently, x ∈ liminf(U) iff x belongs to all but finitely many members of some infinite V ⊆ U. The closure of U under the lim inf operation is the smallest family containing U that is closed under taking lim inf of its infinite subfamilies.
- X has the δ-property if for every open ω-cover U of X, the set X belongs to the closure of U under the lim inf operation (i.e., X can be obtained from U by iterated applications of the lim inf operator).
- X has the property (Ω over Γ) (sometimes denoted ⟨Ω, Γ⟩, also known as the γ-property) if every open ω-cover of X contains a γ-subcover (i.e., an infinite subfamily that is a γ-cover of X).

Question: Are the δ-property and the property (Ω over Γ) equivalent for every set of real numbers X?
artifact.status_search_result: It is known that the property (Ω over Γ) coincides with being a γ-set, and the δ-property defines δ-sets. Orenshtein and Tsaban showed (consistently, under the set-theoretic assumption p = c) that there exists a δ-set that is not a γ-set, by constructing a set of reals A for which C_p(A) has the Pytkeev property but is not Fréchet–Urysohn. Thus the two properties are consistently not equivalent. Whether ZFC alone refutes the equivalence (i.e., whether a δ-set that is not a γ-set can be constructed without additional axioms) appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Linear σ-additivity and some applications
status_evidence.snippet: Under p = c there is a δ-set that is not a γ-set; equivalently, a set of reals A such that C_p(A) is not Fréchet–Urysohn but has the Pytkeev property.
status_evidence.claim: A consistent (under p=c) construction of a δ-set that is not a γ-set shows that the δ-property and (Ω over Γ) are consistently not equivalent.

status_evidence.title: Selection Principles and special sets of reals: Open problems (math/0609601)
status_evidence.snippet: Is the δ-property equivalent to (Ω over Γ)?
status_evidence.claim: The equivalence of the δ-property and (Ω over Γ) is listed as an open problem in the surveyed selection-principles problems.
